speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been present and if it started as a blister or a bump? Also, do you have a history of diabetes, venous insufficiency, or recent trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the specific evolution from a bite site to a painful ulcer strongly points to this inflammatory condition rather than an infection, as it is a classic neutrophilic dermatosis often triggered by trauma (pathergy). I will now request a wound culture to rule out secondary infection before we proceed with topical steroids or systemic therapy.
